rules.title: Prefer Database Constraints Over Application-Level Locking
rules.rule: When database constraints such as exclusion constraints or unique indexes can enforce data integrity, avoid using application-level locks or broad transactions. Rely on database-level errors (e.g., PG::ExclusionViolation) to handle conflicts safely and only wrap operations in transactions when cross-record consistency is truly required.

rules.rule: Do not use deprecated or context-specific helper methods whose behavior is misleading. For account-scoped requests, use explicit helpers such as current_account or current_patients instead of methods like current_user that return an arbitrary record.

rules.title: Guard Against Missing Data in UI Components
rules.rule: When rendering UI components that depend on filtered or conditional data, add guards to handle cases where the selected item is absent from the available options. This prevents crashes when the underlying data set does not include the expected value.

rules.title: Prevent SQL Injection via String Interpolation
rules.rule: Never build SQL fragments by interpolating user input directly into strings, even inside quoted values. Use parameterized queries or ActiveRecord methods so that malicious input cannot break out of the intended clause.

rules.title: Avoid Premature Database Indexes
rules.rule: Do not add database indexes before measuring query performance and understanding data distribution. Existing base-scope indexes may already be sufficient, and unnecessary indexes add write overhead and storage cost.

    add_index :messages, [:patient_id, :created_at]
  end
end

  def change

    # deferred until query volume and EXPLAIN output justify it
  end
end

rules.title: Repository-wide conventions, principles, and critical gotchas
rules.rule:
### Repository-wide conventions and principles

**Project Structure & Locations**
- `app/` — Rails MVC.
- `client/` — React + TypeScript bundle (Mantine, Zustand). New frontend code goes here.
- `app/assets/javascripts/` — legacy raw JS + jQuery. **Do not extend; migrate to `client/` instead.**
- `lib/` — non-Rails Ruby libraries.
- `spec/` — RSpec.
- `db/migrate/` — migrations.
- `config/locales/` — i18n files.
- `doc/physiapp-api/` — AcmeApp API contracts. **Contract-first:** update the contract and get it agreed before implementing an endpoint; keep it in sync in the same PR as serializer changes.

**Critical Gotchas**
- **Always use `bin/docker`, not `docker compose` directly.** The wrapper sets up AWS/sops/1Password env that the containers depend on.
- **Use `data-test-id`**, not the React default `data-testid`. Selectors break otherwise.
- **Never hardcode user-facing strings.** Use `t()` and put copy in `config/locales/`.
- **Encrypted credentials live in `*.enc.yml`** via sops. Never `cat` an `.enc.yml`, never commit decrypted values.
- **Prefer real services in specs over mocks** when the docker container already exists (Redis, Typesense, Postgres). The CI runs them anyway.

**Coding Principles**
- DRY, SOLID, self-documenting names, focused functions.
- Line length ≤ 160.
- Comments only for non-obvious *why*.
- Temporary code awaiting a later cleanup phase gets a greppable tag: `TODO: <EPIC-TAG> remove after <condition>`. One tag per project, so teardown is a single grep.

**Documentation Sync**
- **Update `CODEBASE_MAP.md` whenever features change.** Adding, editing, or removing a feature means updating its feature → directories entry (and the tree, if directories moved) in the same PR.
- **Update the relevant `CLAUDE.md` after a correction.** When the user corrects Claude's output because a convention or gotcha was missing or wrong, capture the fix in the closest `CLAUDE.md`.

**Domain Glossary**
- **User** — anyone who can log in.
- **Practitioner** (= Provider) — Acme web user.
- **Patient** (= Client) — AcmeApp mobile user.
- **Program** (= Protocol) — prescribed exercise program; the core domain model.
- **BrandedApp** — whitelabeled AcmeApp.
- **Exercise IDs in the API are prefixed**: `1…` = system exercise, `2…` = custom exercise. Intentional, not a bug.

**Pull Requests**
- **Always open PRs with the repo template** at `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and fill in every section — link the `WWW-` Jira ticket, explain *what the PR does* for reviewers, add `fixes SENTRY-CODE` if applicable (delete the line otherwise), and complete the author checklist. The GitHub web UI prefills it automatically; with `gh` use `gh pr create --web` or `gh pr create --body-file .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`.

**Code Review**
- Prioritize readability, correctness, long-term maintainability, consistency with surrounding code, and test coverage.
- Prefix comments that must be resolved with `Blocker:`; use `Nit:` / `Drive by:` for the negotiable rest.
- Recurring bug patterns to hunt:
  - Multiple `update!`/writes without a wrapping transaction.
  - `||=` (or other short-circuits) around side-effecting calls in loops.
  - Frontend limits duplicated as literals instead of referencing the backend constant.
- Dead-code removal needs production evidence — a Coverband / Datadog / `_pttss/coverage` link in the PR, not just a clean grep.

rules.title: Controllers: orchestration-only HTTP entry points conventions
rules.rule:
# app/controllers/ — HTTP entry points. Controllers orchestrate; they do not contain business logic.

## Conventions

- **Strong parameters always.** Define a private `*_params` method per action; never pass raw `params` to a model.
- **No business logic.** Call into `app/services/` or `app/interactors/` for anything beyond CRUD-and-render. If a controller action grows past a few lines of orchestration, extract.
- **Look for an existing service before writing search/filter/pagination logic.** Extend the existing abstraction rather than reimplementing it inline in the controller.
- **No raw SQL.** Use ActiveRecord scopes; if a complex query is needed, put it in `app/scopes/` and call it from the controller.
- **Sanitize user input** before persisting or rendering. Rails' default helpers (`sanitize`, `strip_tags`, parameterized queries) are the canonical defense against XSS and SQL injection.
- **i18n via `t()`** for flash messages, error responses, redirects with copy.
- **CanCanCan for authorization** — `Ability` lives in `app/models/ability.rb`, with sub-app variants in `app/models/direct_app/`, `app/models/crm/`, `app/models/cms/`. Call `authorize! :action, resource` early in actions; never gate by hand-rolled role checks.

## New endpoint: Grape or plain controller?

Two frameworks coexist. Grape serves JSON API contracts; plain ActionController serves browser surfaces (HTML pages, session-based flows). Pick by consumer:

| You are building | Framework | Location | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON endpoint for AcmeApp clients (mobile + web) | Grape | `app/controllers/api/physi_app/` — newest applicable version (v3 default; v4 only for dynamic-session endpoints, see `doc/physiapp-api/README.md`) | OAuth2 (`API::Shared::OAuth2`) |
| Provider-facing public API | Grape | `app/controllers/api/v3/` | OAuth2 |
| PMS/partner sync (token-based) | Grape | `app/controllers/api/{pms_api,companies,import}/`, `app/api/` | Token header / HTTP Basic |
| Practitioner web page (HTML/JSON for the Panel) | Plain controller | `app/controllers/pt/` | Devise session + CanCanCan |
| Patient web page | Plain controller | `app/controllers/physi_app/` | Devise session |
| Browser OAuth / iframe partner flow | Plain controller | `app/controllers/pt/jane_sdk/`, `app/controllers/api/iframe/`, … | Session / OAuth PKCE |

Mechanically: Grape APIs are `mount`ed in `routes.rb` and use the Grape param DSL + `API::Shared` error handling; plain controllers are routed via `namespace`/`resources` and use strong params.

**Legacy — don't extend:** `app/controllers/api/pms/` (browser-session PMS API, superseded by the Jane SDK) and AcmeApp API v2.

## API controllers (Grape)

Grape-specific conventions (deprecation lifecycle, pagination, 422 format) live in `app/controllers/api/CLAUDE.md`. Repo-wide rules:

- Prefer serializers in `app/serializers/` over inline `render json:` hashes.
- **Declare Grape params in snake_case.** A shared request concern rewrites incoming keys to snake_case before validation (grep `deep_transform_keys`), so a camelCase `requires`/`optional` declaration never matches and the param is silently dropped.
- **API changes are additive.** New fields go alongside existing ones. Removing a field requires that released mobile app versions no longer read it, verified on staging. Update the contract in `doc/physiapp-api/` in the same PR.

## Tests

- **Endpoint specs — Grape and plain controllers alike — are request specs** under `spec/requests/`, mirroring the mount/route path (e.g. `spec/requests/api/physi_app/v4/…`), `type: :request`.
- **Unit specs of Grape helpers/action classes** mirror the app path (currently under `spec/controllers/api/…` because that's where the classes live — they are unit specs, not controller specs).
- `type: :controller` specs are legacy; `spec/controllers/` and `spec/api/` get no new endpoint specs. See `spec/CLAUDE.md`.

examples.snippet:
def create
  Service::CreateThing.call(thing_params)
  redirect_to things_path, notice: t('.created')
end

private

def thing_params
  params.require(:thing).permit(:name, :value)
end

def create
  Thing.create(params[:thing])
  redirect_to things_path, notice: 'Created!'
end

rules.title: API Controllers Conventions and Standards
rules.rule:
### API Versioning
New AcmeApp endpoints must go on **v3** by default. v4 is not a full replacement; it exists only for the dynamic server-side program-session redesign. Only endpoints affected by that move to v4; everything else stays on v2/v3. v2 is legacy — do not add endpoints there.

### Deprecating an Endpoint
Use the `deprecated_endpoint` helper (available in every Grape API via `API::Shared::Errors`).

```ruby
get "/" do
  deprecated_endpoint("v3-programs") do
    { programs: [] }
  end
end
```

**Lifecycle**: monitoring → stub → 404 → removal
1. Wrap the real implementation in `deprecated_endpoint` to start logging traffic.
2. Replace the real implementation with a static stub once ready to stop serving real data.
3. Enable the Flipper flag for the endpoint name via the Flipper UI to return 404 to all clients.
4. After confirming clients have stopped hitting it, remove the endpoint entirely.

**Naming**: Use a stable slug identifying the resource and version, e.g., `"v3-programs"`, `"v2-exercises-submit"`. Do not change this string as it is the Flipper actor and changing it resets flag state.

**Context**: Pass per-endpoint context to the log using `context: { ... }`. Avoid logging sensitive values like tokens or passwords.

```ruby
deprecated_endpoint("v3-programs", context: { patient_id: params[:id] }) do
  { programs: [] }
end
```

### Pagination (New Endpoints)
Pagination uses an **opaque, base64-encoded JSON `pageToken`**. The client treats it as a black box and echoes back `nextPageToken` / `prevPageToken`.

- **Request params**:
  - `pageToken` (optional, omit for the first page).
  - `perPage` (optional) — client sets it on the **first** request only; ignored on subsequent requests because it's encoded in the token. Default to **20** and cap at **100** using `DEFAULT_PER_PAGE` / `MAX_PER_PAGE`.
- **Encode/Decode**: Use `Pagination::PageToken.encode(...)` / `Pagination::PageToken.decode(...)` (`app/services/pagination/page_token.rb`). The token **must** carry `per_page` (it is the source of truth). `page` (or cursor) is optional and defaults to the first page when absent.
- **Response**: Carries a `meta` object — `{ nextPageToken, prevPageToken, total }` — with `nextPageToken`/`prevPageToken` set to `null` when there is no next/previous page.

```json
{
  "templates": [ /* ... */ ],
  "meta": { "nextPageToken": "eyJwYWdlIjoyfQ==", "prevPageToken": null, "total": 42 }
}
```

### Validation Errors (422, New Endpoints)
Failed validations (`422` only) return an `errors` array containing `full_message` (translated error message), `field` (may be nested like `"exercises[0][name]"`, defaults to `"base"`), and `type` (error type, persisted, not translated).

```json
{ "errors": [ { "field": "email", "full_message": "Ten email jest zajęty", "type": "taken" } ] }
```

Use existing concerns rather than hand-rolling the shape:
- `API::AcmeApp::V3::ActiveRecordErrorsFormatter#format_active_record_errors` for model validation errors (`app/controllers/concerns/api/physi_app/v3/active_record_errors_formatter.rb`). Example: `error!({ errors: format_active_record_errors(result.errors) }, 422)`.
- `API::AcmeApp::V3::GrapeErrorFormatter` for Grape param-validation errors (`app/controllers/concerns/api/physi_app/v3/grape_error_formatter.rb`).

examples.snippet:
# Incorrect: adding a new endpoint to v2
namespace 'v2' do
  get '/new_feature' do
    # ...
  end
end

rules.title: Domain Organizers Conventions in app/domains
rules.rule:
### Domain Organizers Conventions

- **One module per domain**: Each domain must be namespaced under the domain noun (e.g., `Billing`, `Protocols`, `APIEvents`). It acts as the layer between models and controllers/jobs. How the module exposes the concept (class methods, nested classes, value objects) is a per-domain call with no mandated public-surface shape.
- **Multi-step logic**: New multi-step logic must go in a service (`app/services/`). Do NOT add new interactors. The `interactor` gem (`include Interactor`, `delegate … to: :context`, `context.fail!`) is legacy and only lives in existing domains; modify those in place if needed.
- **Value objects**: Must be plain Ruby. They should have a `.for(record)` constructor, memoized collaborators (e.g., `@_subscription ||= …`), and query methods. Refer to `billing/duration.rb`.
- **i18n and Errors**: Use `I18n.t` for any user-facing string. Use `Sentry.capture_exception` when you swallow an error rather than re-raise it.
- **Naming**: The module must be named after the domain noun. Files must be snake_case mirroring the constant path (Zeitwerk). Nested concerns must live in subdirectories with their own module nesting (e.g., `APIEvents::Interactors::LogNewClientCreatedEvent`).
- **Tests**: Test files must be located at `spec/domains/<domain>/…_spec.rb` mirroring the tree. Assert that the root module delegates to the right nested class. Use factory_bot and spy/`have_received` for collaborators.

rules.title: Interactors conventions and legacy status
rules.rule:
# Interactors (Legacy Pattern - Do Not Create New)

Multi-step business workflows in `app/interactors/` coordinate several steps (and often several services) toward one user-facing outcome. They use the `interactor` gem.

## Core Conventions (Shared with `app/services`)
- No metaprogramming.
- No concerns/mixins.
- Prefer ActiveRecord over raw SQL.
- Business logic belongs here (or in services), not in ActiveRecord models.

## Result Objects & Mechanics
- `include Interactor`
- Define instance method `#call`
- Assign outputs onto `context`
- Signal failure with `context.fail!`
- `.call` returns an `Interactor::Context`; callers check `.success?` and read attributes off it.

```ruby
class CreatePatientTransfer
  include Interactor
  delegate :current_user, :patient, :params, to: :context

  def call
    context.transfer = transfer
    context.fail! unless valid_transfer? && transfer.save
  end
end

# caller
interaction = CreatePatientTransfer.call(current_user: current_user, patient: patient, params: params)
render json: { error: interaction.transfer.errors } unless interaction.success?
```

## Failure Handling
- `context.fail!(error: "...")` attaches data the caller can read off the failed context.
- Use `context.fail!` for expected domain failures.
- Use `raise` only for unexpected failures.
- See `create_patient_transfer.rb` for an example.

## Legacy Status
- **Do not create new interactors.**
- New multi-step logic goes in a service (`app/services/`).
- Touch an interactor only to modify existing behaviour.
- Do not rewrite a working interactor into a service just for consistency (avoid needless churn).

## Tests
- Spec files go in `spec/interactors/<namespace>/<class_name>_spec.rb`.
- Stub collaborator services with spy + `have_received`, then assert each step ran.
- See `spec/CLAUDE.md` for more details.

examples.snippet:
class CreatePatientTransfer
  include Interactor
  delegate :current_user, :patient, :params, to: :context

  def call
    context.transfer = transfer
    context.fail! unless valid_transfer? && transfer.save
  end
end

# caller
interaction = CreatePatientTransfer.call(current_user: current_user, patient: patient, params: params)
render json: { error: interaction.transfer.errors } unless interaction.success?

# New interactor created for new logic (should be a service instead)
class NewBusinessWorkflow
  include Interactor
  def call; end
end

rules.title: ActionMailer conventions and standards
rules.rule:
## ActionMailer Conventions

### Inheritance & Base Setup
- **Inherit from `AppMailer`** (`< ActionMailer::Base`): layout `"email"`, registers `PreventMailInterceptor` (no delivery outside production), `default from: noreply_email_from`, plus `multipart_mail` / `with_locale`.
- Domain bases extend `AppMailer` — e.g. `PatientMailer::BaseMailer` adds branding vars + the AcmeApp layout.

### Delivery Methods
- Async sends go through `app/tasks/` jobs using `deliver_later`.
- Transactional emails use `deliver_now`.

### Locale Handling
- **Wrap subject AND body in `with_locale(user)`** so the recipient's locale drives rendering:

```ruby
class UserMailer < AppMailer
  def unlock_account_notification(user, token)
    @user, @token = user, token
    with_locale(@user) { mail(to: @user.email, subject: t("devise.mailer.unlock_instructions.subject")) }
  end
end
```

### Subjects
- Subjects must use `t("emails.<domain>.<action>.subject", …)` — copy lives in `config/locales/**/acme.yml` under `emails:`. **Never hardcode** subject strings.

### Views
- Views colocate in `app/views/<mailer>/<action>.{html,text}.erb`.
- Method name must match the view filename.
- `multipart_mail` renders both HTML and text formats.

### Attachments
- Use `attachments["program.pdf"] = file.read`.

### Branding / Whitelabel
- Use `AcmeApp::Branding::App.determine(provider)` for subject prefixes, logos, and app titles.

### Naming
- Pattern: `{Domain}Mailer`.
- Namespaced where scoped, e.g. `PatientMailer::MessagesMailer`, `Crm::UserMailer`.

### Tests
- Spec files in `spec/mailers/…_spec.rb`.
- Reuse `shared_examples "a mailer"` from `spec/support/mailer.rb`, which asserts delivery, recipient, and rendering across every available locale.
- See `spec/CLAUDE.md` for additional test conventions.

examples.snippet: with_locale(@user) { mail(to: @user.email, subject: t("devise.mailer.unlock_instructions.subject")) }
mail(to: @user.email, subject: "Unlock your account")

rules.title: ActiveRecord Model Conventions
rules.rule:
Models must contain only persistence-related concerns (validations, associations, and basic data management). No business logic should be placed in models; it belongs in `app/services/`.

Key conventions:
- **Validations and associations** are the model's job. Keep them here.
- **Callbacks** (`before_save`/`after_commit`) should be used only when necessary (e.g., maintaining a denormalized column or sanitizing input). Do not use callbacks for external side effects like emails, jobs, or API calls. Prefer explicit calls in services.
- **Queries**: Use ActiveRecord methods (scopes, `where`/`joins`/`merge`) instead of raw SQL. If a query is AR-unfriendly, put it in `app/scopes/` as a named query object, not in the model.
- **Security**: Never interpolate user input into a query. Use bind variables (`where("foo = ?", val)` or hash form).
- **Naming**: Follow Zeitwerk autoloader naming conventions (e.g., `app/models/branded_app/config.rb` maps to `BrandedApp::Config`). File path must match constant path.
- **Schema**: `ignored_columns` is a temporary precaution, not permanent hygiene. Remove it once the column is gone.
- **STI / Polymorphic**: Avoid adding new Single Table Inheritance (STI) hierarchies; prefer composition. Existing ones are fine to extend.
- **Tests**: Place tests in `spec/models/<model>_spec.rb`. Test validations, associations, scopes, and persistence-related callbacks. Behavior tests go on the driving service.

examples.snippet: where("foo = #{val}")
where("foo = ?", val)
after_commit :send_welcome_email # External side effect in callback

# In app/services/user_signup.rb
user.save!
Mailer.send_welcome_email(user)

rules.title: Policy Objects Conventions
rules.rule:
Policy objects in `app/policies/` are plain business-rule predicate objects that answer domain questions (e.g., 'can this protocol repeat?', 'can this provider be removed?') and are instantiated directly at the call site.

**Not an authorization framework:**
These policies are **not Pundit and not CanCanCan**, despite the `*Policy` name. App-wide authorization is CanCanCan: `Ability` (`app/models/ability.rb`, `include CanCan::Ability`) with `authorize!` in controllers. Do not add a Pundit `Scope` class or expect a policy-lookup mechanism here — there is none.

**Conventions:**
- **PORO, no base class.** Constructor takes domain objects; public methods are predicates.
- **Surface *why* with `ActiveModel::Errors`** when the caller needs the reason (i18n messages), not just a boolean — see `content_copying_policy.rb`.
- **Optional `.allowed?` / `.for` class factories** for one-line call sites.
- **`Flipper.enabled?(:flag, user)`** where a rule is feature-flagged. `I18n.t` for any message.

**Naming:**
`{Concept}Policy`, namespaced by domain (e.g., `Company::RemoveProviderFromCompanyPolicy`, `DirectApp::AdminAccessPolicy`).

**Tests:**
`spec/policies/…_spec.rb` — instantiate directly and assert the predicates (`expect(policy).to be_repeatable`). No Pundit matchers. See `spec/CLAUDE.md`.

examples.snippet:
class RepeatableProtocolPolicy
  def initialize(protocol)
    @protocol = protocol
  end

  def repeatable?
    return false unless protocol&.provider && Billing::Status.for(protocol.provider).practitioner_access?

    protocol.repeat_week? && active? && protocol.total_weeks < Rails.application.config.max_program_weeks
  end
end

class RepeatableProtocolPolicy < ApplicationPolicy
  class Scope
    # ...
  end
end

rules.title: Serializer Patterns and Conventions
rules.rule:
Serializers in this codebase follow three coexisting patterns. Match the pattern already used in the area being edited. 

## Choosing a pattern (new serializers)
- **Default — a plain Ruby object (PORO).** This is the current direction: most serializers added since 2023 are hand-rolled, no gem. Take the record (and optional `scope`) in `initialize` and expose `as_json`; aggregate/props objects instead use a `.call` that returns a frozen Hash.
- **`ActiveModel::Serializer` is legacy — don't add new ones.** The `active_model_serializers` gem is unmaintained; it still backs the largest existing web/PT/admin surface (`ApplicationSerializer < ActiveModel::Serializer` + audience sub-bases, `attributes` DSL). Modify those in place; new serializers should be POROs.
- **Mobile `api/v3/` uses the `jsonapi-serializer` gem.** Files there extend `API::V3::BaseSerializer` (`include JSONAPI::Serializer`) — stay consistent within `api/v3/`. It is not the choice for new work elsewhere.

## Naming
`{Concept}Serializer`, namespaced by audience/version (`PatientAPI::V3::ProtocolSerializer`, `Pt::Reports::…`). Props/aggregate POROs may drop the suffix (`…Props`, `…Data`). File path mirrors the constant path. Use `I18n.l` / explicit time-zone conversion for dates.

## Tests
`spec/serializers/…_spec.rb` — assert the output hash shape and custom logic (nil handling, key casing, date formatting), not the framework. See `spec/CLAUDE.md`.

examples.snippet:
class NewSerializer < ActiveModel::Serializer
  attributes :id, :title
end

rules.title: Service Object Conventions in app/services/
rules.rule:
Service objects in `app/services/` must follow these conventions:

- **Plain Ruby class with a `.call` class-method entry point (keyword args) that builds the object and delegates to an instance.** No `ApplicationService` base class, no module mixed in. The signature is the contract:

```ruby
module Patients
  class Invite
    def self.call(patient:, inviter:, notifier: Notifier.new(patient))
      new(patient:, inviter:, notifier:).call
    end

    def initialize(patient:, inviter:, notifier:)
      @patient = patient
      @inviter = inviter
      @notifier = notifier
    end

    def call
      @notifier.deliver # ...
    end
  end
end
```

- **No metaprogramming.** No `define_method`, no `send(:"#{prefix}_..."`, no method names built from strings. Use explicit `case` or a constant hash if you need dispatch.
- **No concerns, no mixins.** Prefer object composition — extract a collaborator class, pass it in.
- **Methods private by default.** Only `.call` is public.
- **ActiveRecord, not raw SQL.** If you need a window function or other AR-unfriendly query, isolate it in a query object under `app/scopes/` or `app/services/queries/`, not inline in the service.
- **No business logic in `app/models/`.** That logic belongs here.
- **i18n via `t()`** for any user-facing string the service produces (errors, notification copy).
- **Naming:** Namespace under the domain noun (`Patients::Invite`, `Programs::Duplicate`). Verb-first class name describes the action.
- **Result objects:** Return nested `Success`/`Failure` Structs the caller checks with `.success?`. No shared base class, no gem:

```ruby
class TransferProtocolToProviderService
  Success = Struct.new { def success? = true }
  Failure = Struct.new(:errors, keyword_init: true) { def success? = false }
  # ... Success.new / Failure.new(errors: [...])
end
```

`Success` may carry a payload (`Struct.new(:colleague, keyword_init: true)`). Use `errors:` (array of localized strings — they flow to the frontend) or `error:` (single object, typically a named error). See `transfer_protocol_to_provider_service.rb`, `colleagues_company/add_colleague.rb`.

The error shape follows the caller's context: controller-facing services carry `errors:` localized strings (optionally a `status:`/`error_code:` symbol) for the controller or serializer to render; service-to-service failures carry a symbol code on `error:`/`error_code:` so the caller can branch on it (`company/move_provider.rb`). Don't branch on `result.error.is_a?(...)` — use a symbol code when the caller must distinguish failures. An error object carrying a localized `.message` for the caller to render is an accepted existing pattern (`reports/review.rb`). `raise` is reserved for genuinely unexpected conditions.

- **SQL fragments:** Never interpolate values or column names into SQL strings — pass every dynamic fragment (even an `ORDER BY`) through `sanitize_sql_array`, or `Arel.sql` with bind variables.

- **Non-service POROs:** Sometimes a namespace needs supporting objects that don't own a single action — they model a domain concept, transform data, or encapsulate a rule. These live alongside services in the same namespace directory (e.g. `app/services/physi_app/assignment/exercise_session.rb`). No `.call` requirement. Shape them to fit their purpose: initializer with keyword args, instance methods, whatever makes the object clear.

**Naming for non-service POROs:** noun-first (`ExerciseSession`, `SessionConverter`) when the instance is reused across calls; verb-first (`FetchAssignments`, `StatusCheck`) when it's invoked once like a function.

- **Tests:** `spec/services/<namespace>/<class_name>_spec.rb`. Use factory_bot, spy + `have_received` for collaborators. No `let`. See `spec/CLAUDE.md`.

examples.snippet:
class Patients::Invite < ApplicationService
  def call
    # ...
  end
end

rules.title: ERB View Templates: Keep Dumb, Use React for New UI, and Follow Tag/Convention Standards
rules.rule:
ERB templates in `app/views/` must remain dumb (formatting and composition only, no logic).

**New UI and Feature Rules:**
- New UI goes in React, not new ERB. For a new feature, add a React component under `client/` rather than a new server-rendered view here.
- `app/assets/javascripts/` is legacy — do not extend it.
- Editing existing ERB to maintain a current server-rendered screen is acceptable.

**ERB Tag Usage:**
| Tag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<% ... %>` | Ruby without output |
| `<%= ... %>` | Ruby with output (HTML-escaped) |
| `<%# ... %>` | Comments |
| `<%- ... -%>` | Whitespace control |

**Conventions:**
- **Use partials for reusable components:**
  ```erb
  <%= render partial: "shared/user_card", locals: { user: @user } %>
  <%= render partial: "shared/user_card", collection: @users, as: :user %>
  ```
- **`content_for` + `yield` for layout sections:**
  ```erb
  <% content_for :head do %>
    <meta name="description" content="<%= @page_description %>">
  <% end %>
  ```
- **Helpers, not templates, hold logic.** If writing more than a one-line conditional in ERB, move it to `app/helpers/` (or a presenter / view object).
- **Sanitize before rendering.** Any user-provided string going out via `raw`, `html_safe`, or `sanitize` must be reviewed for XSS. Default `<%= %>` is escaped — keep it that way.
- **i18n via `t()`.** Never hardcode user-facing strings. Keys live in `config/locales/`.
- **`data-test-id` (not `data-testid`)** for any element a Capybara feature spec selects on.

**Tests:**
- Views are exercised through feature specs (`spec/features/`) or request specs (`spec/requests/`). Do not write standalone view specs.

examples.snippet: <%= render partial: "shared/user_card", locals: { user: @user } %>

<% if current_user.admin? && @post.published? && @post.author_id == current_user.id %>
  <%= @post.title %>
<% end %>

rules.title: Zustand Store and Bundle Management Rules
rules.rule:
Per-product React bundles in `client/app/bundles/` must adhere to the following Zustand store conventions:

- **Named Store Hooks**: Each bundle has its own named store hook. Use the named hook, not a generic `useStore`:
  - `useAcmeStore` — `pt/` bundle
  - `usePtDirectStore` — `direct_app/` bundle
  - `useSharedStore` — `shared/` bundle
  - (each bundle defines its own)

- **Adding a slice**:
  1. Create the slice at `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/storeSlices/<sliceName>.{ts,js}`.
  2. Export it from `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/storeSlices/index.{ts,js}`.
  3. Wire it into `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/store.{ts,js}`.

- **Consuming the store**: Destructure the selectors you need; do not subscribe to the whole store.

- **State updates**:
  - Use **`immer`** for nested updates — `set(produce(draft => ...))`. Don't hand-roll deep clones.
  - Keep slices small. If a slice exceeds ~200 lines, split it.

- **Migrating from Redux**:
  - When touching a Redux-backed class component:
    1. Wrap the class component in a functional wrapper that reads from the Zustand store.
    2. Pass Zustand state down as props until the class component can be converted.
    3. Eventually convert the class component to a function component and drop the wrapper.
  - Do not add new Redux slices — Zustand only.

examples.snippet: const state = useAcmeStore(); // Subscribing to the whole store is prohibited

rules.title: I18n Locale Management and Translation Standards
rules.rule:
Every user-facing string in the app must resolve to i18n YAML files in `config/locales/`.

## General Rules
- **Never hardcode a user-facing string** in Ruby, ERB, or React. Always use `t(".key")` (Ruby/ERB) or the equivalent in the frontend i18n layer.
- **PR Review**: Reject any string literal in a controller/view/component that a translator would need to localize.
- **File naming**: Use `en.yml`, `<feature>.en.yml`, or a directory tree mirroring the area. Match the existing structure before inventing a new layout.

## Key Naming
- Lazy lookup (`t(".foo")`) is preferred in views and controllers — the key resolves against the current controller/action path.
- For shared strings, use explicit dotted keys: `t("shared.confirmations.delete")`.
- Keep key paths shallow when possible. Deep nesting (≥ 4 levels) makes search painful.

## Adding a Translation
1. Add the key to the relevant `*.en.yml`.
2. Reference it from the calling code.
3. Automatically translate `pl`, `es`, `ja`, `ko`, `fi`, `ro` locales.
4. **Do not** add other locales by hand — leave them missing for the translator workflow.
5. Run `i18n-tasks normalize` to ensure the key is properly formatted.

## Translation Rules
The app is a platform for physiotherapists and their patients; translate with that audience in mind.
- **Never translate product names**: Acme, AcmeApp, AcmeAssistant.
- **Preserve HTML markup** — do not modify any text enclosed in `< >` characters.
- **Keep interpolation placeholders** (`%{variable}`) intact and correctly positioned so the sentence stays grammatical.
- **Avoid structures requiring grammatical gender agreement with a placeholder.** Never let a verb or adjective agree with `%{variable}` — e.g., Polish `"%{metric_name}" jest przedstawiony jako %{chart_type}` fails for feminine nouns; write `Metryka "%{metric_name}" jest przedstawiona jako %{chart_type}` instead. Rephrase completely if needed.
- **Keep placeholders in the nominative case.** If a declined form seems required, restructure the sentence so the placeholder stays nominative; if unavoidable, adjust the surrounding words.
- **Prioritize natural fluency over literal translation** — restructure or split sentences to sound idiomatic.
- **Finnish terminology**: Use `asiakas` (not `potilas`) for patient, `ohjelmaeditori` (not `ohjelman luoja`) for program editor, and `frekvenssi` (not `tiheys`) for frequency.

## What Lives Elsewhere
- Validation message overrides: Still in locale files, under `activerecord:` / `activemodel:`.
- Email templates: Strings in locale files, layout in `app/views/mailers/`.
- Routes: Do not go through i18n — URL slugs are English.

examples.snippet: flash[:notice] = "Profile updated successfully"

# config/locales/en.yml
# en:
#   profiles:
#     update:
#       notice: "Profile updated successfully"

# app/controllers/profiles_controller.rb
flash[:notice] = t(".notice")

rules.title: Database Migration Safety, Performance, and Style Standards
rules.rule:
## Safety rules

- **Index changes on large tables: `algorithm: :concurrently`** + `disable_ddl_transaction!` at the top of the migration. Standard `add_index` takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock.

  ruby
  class AddIndexToPatientsOnEmail < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.0]
    disable_ddl_transaction!

    def change
      add_index :patients, :email, algorithm: :concurrently
    end
  end
  

- **`NOT NULL` on existing columns: two migrations.** First add the column with a default, backfill in batches via a MaintenanceTask, then add the `NOT NULL` constraint as `NOT VALID` + validate concurrently — never `change_column_null` on a large existing table in one shot.
- **Data backfills are not migrations.** If the change doesn't alter DB structure, write a MaintenanceTask (`app/tasks/maintenance/`, `maintenance_tasks` gem) instead — it gives batching, progress tracking and pause/resume, and keeps deploys fast.
- **`add_column` with a default**: safe on Postgres 11+ for static defaults (instant), but a *function* default still rewrites the table — avoid.
- **Foreign keys**: add with `validate: false`, then validate in a separate migration.
- **Renames**: avoid for hot tables. Add the new column, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, drop the old column over multiple deploys.
- **Check DB views before renaming/dropping a column.** Views selecting from the table break silently (and their models can't `ignored_columns` around it) — update the view in its own staged migration.

## Perf migrations: measure before AND after

For migrations that add/change indexes or rewrite queries for performance, capture `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of the affected query **before** the migration and **after** the migration. Both numbers go in the PR description. A migration without comparable before/after numbers is incomplete.

Run against a representative dataset — production replica or a seeded staging snapshot, not a 10-row dev DB.

## Style

- One migration = one logical change. Don't bundle a column add with an index add unless they are inseparable.
- Use `change` over `up`/`down` when reversible; use `up`/`down` when not.
- Migration filenames are timestamp-prefixed by Rails; let the generator pick the timestamp.

## Tests

Migrations themselves are tested via `bin/docker exec dev bin/rspec spec/migrations/` when they have data transforms. Schema changes are validated by the rest of the suite running green after migration.

examples.snippet: add_index :patients, :email

disable_ddl_transaction!

def change
  add_index :patients, :email, algorithm: :concurrently
end

rules.title: Search Infrastructure Conventions (lib/search/)
rules.rule:
# Search Infrastructure Conventions (lib/search/)

## Typesense
- **Config is environment-scoped:** The hybrid-search Typesense config currently applies to non-prod environments only — confirm the env gate before assuming a setting is global.
- **Distance threshold:** The distance threshold for hybrid (vector + keyword) search lives in the search config; touching it changes recall for every consumer. Don't tune it without an A/B plan.

## `ClientWrapper.upsert` — wipe-vs-merge semantics
- **`ClientWrapper.upsert` replaces the entire document** at the given ID — it does not merge fields. If two background jobs both write to the same document, each writing a different subset of fields, the second write **wipes** the first job's fields.
- Before splitting writes for one document across jobs, confirm one of the following:
  1. The jobs touch disjoint documents, **or**
  2. The writes are serialized (e.g. all funnel through one indexer), **or**
  3. You're doing a true full-document upsert from a single source of truth.
- If none of those hold, you have a write race that will silently lose data in production.

## Testing
- **Use a real Typesense container, not mocks.** Docker-compose provides `typesense` in dev and CI.
- E2E request specs hit the real container.
- Unit-level specs that need a fast inner loop can spy on `ClientWrapper` calls and assert the **arguments**, but the integration boundary itself must be tested against real Typesense.

## Algolia
- Legacy. Don't add new Algolia-backed indexes — migrate to Typesense. Existing Algolia code paths are maintenance only.

## Adding a search index
1. Define the collection schema under `lib/search/typesense/schemas/`.
2. Register a sync job that emits via `ClientWrapper.upsert` (or batched `import`).
3. Add an integration spec against the real container.
4. If hybrid (vector) search: confirm the embedding model and distance threshold.

rules.title: RSpec Testing Standards for Backend
rules.rule:
## Test Taxonomy & Pyramid

Follow a strict test pyramid:
- **Unit specs (base, most numerous)** — `spec/{models,services,interactors,policies,serializers,domains,tasks,decorators,forms,presenters,validators,…}/`. One class in isolation. Fast.
- **Request specs (middle)** — `spec/requests/`. End-to-end but scoped to the HTTP/API boundary.
- **Feature specs (top, fewest)** — `spec/features/`. End-to-end through a real browser; golden-path only, slow.

Rule of thumb: push coverage **down** the pyramid — prove a branch in a unit spec, not a feature spec, when you can.

## Discipline

- **Avoid `let` / `let!` and large `before` blocks.** They scatter setup and break the arrange/act/assert flow. Inline the setup in each `it` — duplication is fine, *clarity* is the goal.
- **Use `factory_bot` for setup.** Prefer `build`/`build_stubbed` over `create` when persistence isn't needed.
- **Spy + `have_received`** for collaborator interactions; keeps arrange/act/assert linear.
- **One assertion per test** when practical. Multiple `expect` lines are fine if they all describe the same behavior.
- **Assert whole payloads, not fragments.** When a spec checks a serialized response or hash, compare the complete expected body with exact equality (`eq`) — not `include` / `contain_exactly` / single-attribute checks. Freeze time and write literal timestamps into the expected hash. Partial matchers hide accidental shape changes.
- **Descriptive `it` names.** Test names describe the expected behavior, not the method called.
- **Test behavior, not implementation.** Assert observable outcomes and the class's own decisions (cache key, TTL, short-circuit / fail-open branches), not private mechanics — and never that the *framework* works (e.g. don't assert `Rails.cache` memoizes or that `Faraday.new` got an option). Treat framework objects as spied collaborators.
- **Realistic fixtures.** Mirror production shape: request bodies carry every field the real client sends; embedding fixtures use real dims (Cohere v3 = 1024); mutation tests assert **additively** (new field present AND originals unchanged).
- **Cover edge cases and error branches**, not just the happy path.
- **Never trust a spec you haven't seen fail.** Write it red-first, or revert-check it after: would it still pass with the change reverted? If the asserted value can arrive without the code under test (a DB trigger, a column default, `nil` on both sides), it isn't testing anything.
- **Literal fixtures, not generative loops.** Create records with explicit `create`/`build` calls, not loops or helper logic that itself needs verifying.

## Example

ruby
describe User do
  it "logs an invitation record after inviting user" do
    user = build(:user)                # arrange

    user.invite!                        # act

    expect(Invitations.count).to eq(1)  # assert
  end
end
``n
## Unit Specs

The default for any class not covered by a request or feature spec. A good unit spec:

- Tests the internal logic and public behavior of **one class**; everything else is a collaborator.
- **Isolates the class from its collaborators** — stub the app classes/services/jobs it calls and assert interactions with spy + `have_received`; don't reach through to real collaborator behavior.
- **Reconciles with "Real services over mocks"**: stub *collaborator objects*, but keep the *datastore* real — Postgres via `factory_bot` (`build`/`build_stubbed` when persistence isn't needed), real Redis/Typesense; never add fake gems. Stub **only** genuine external boundaries (AWS Bedrock, payment gateways, third-party HTTP).
- Tests the class's **own decisions and branches** (happy path, edge cases, error branches), not private-method mechanics and not the framework.
- Is **fast and deterministic** — no network, no unfrozen time, no unseeded randomness.

## Request Specs > Controller Specs

For HTTP API coverage, write **request specs** under `spec/requests/`. Controller specs are legacy.

## Real Services Over Mocks

When the docker-compose stack already provides the dependency, **use the real service**:

- **Postgres** — always real, via the dev container.
- **Redis** — real, via the `redis` service. Don't add `mock_redis`.
- **Typesense** — real, via the `typesense` service. Don't stub `Typesense::Client`.

The CI runs against the same real services. Adding a mock layer that drifts from prod behavior has burned us before.

## Determinism (No Flaky Tests)

The suite runs in **random order** (`config.order = :random`, `spec/spec_helper.rb`) in a multi-job CI, so non-deterministic tests fail intermittently.

- **Freeze time** — use `freeze_time` / `travel_to` (`ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers`, globally included); never assert against live `Time.now` / `Time.zone.now` / `Date.today`. (Legacy specs use `Timecop`; follow locally if a file already does, but prefer the Rails helpers for new specs.)
- **No randomness in assertions** — don't let `rand` / `SecureRandom` / sampled data drive pass/fail. Using `SecureRandom.hex` purely for **uniqueness** (e.g. a unique fixture name or cache key) is fine; asserting on a random value is not.
- **Independent & isolated** — no shared mutable state or order dependence; clean external state in `before`/`after` (`redis.flushdb`, truncate) since the real containers persist across examples.
- **No `sleep`** — rely on Capybara auto-waiting (`has_*?` predicates) in feature specs; never hard-sleep to "wait for" async work.

## Running

bash
bin/docker exec dev bin/rspec                     # full suite
bin/docker exec dev bin/rspec spec/services/foo_spec.rb  # one file
bin/docker exec dev bin/rspec spec/services/foo_spec.rb:42  # one example
``n
## Scoping

After editing `app/services/foo.rb`, run `spec/services/foo_spec.rb` first; only run the full suite when changing shared concerns (`lib/`, `app/models/concerns/`, initializers).

examples.snippet:
describe User do
  it "logs an invitation record after inviting user" do
    user = build(:user)
    user.invite!
    expect(Invitations.count).to eq(1)
  end
end

describe User do
  let(:user) { create(:user) }
  before { allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_return(nil) }

  it "works" do
    expect(user.invite!).to be_truthy
  end
end

rules.title: Feature spec conventions: PageObject pattern, selectors, and performance guidelines
rules.rule:
## PageObject Pattern

Wrap each page or modal in a PageObject under `spec/support/page_object/`. Tests interact with the PageObject, not raw Capybara matchers — this isolates DOM details from test logic.

- Inherit from `PageObject::Base`.
- Predicate methods are named `has_*?` so Capybara's auto-waiting kicks in.
- **No waiting/retry logic in page objects** — the `has_*?` matchers already wait. If a flow has no positive signal to assert (e.g. after a save), add one to the app (flash/toast) instead of polling for the absence of activity.

Example:
```ruby
module PageObject
  class NewPatientModal < Base
    include Warden::Test::Helpers

    def fill_new_patient_data(first_name, last_name, yob)
      within("#new_patient") do
        fill_in("patient_first_name", with: first_name)
        fill_in("patient_last_name",  with: last_name)
        fill_in("patient_birth_year", with: yob)
      end
    end

    def has_modal_opened?
      has_css?("#new_patient")
    end
  end
end
```

## Selectors

- **`data-test-id` only** for new selectors. (Not `data-testid` — React default differs from our convention.)
- Avoid selecting by raw class or generated ID — they break under refactors.
- **No identifying data (emails, names) in `data-test-id` values** — scope with a stable test-id and assert the text inside it (`has_css?("[data-test-id=row]", text: email)`).

## Live Session Debugging

Browser is exposed at `http://localhost:4444` while a feature spec is paused. Use to debug visually.

## Screenshots

```ruby
save_screenshot("debugging_modal.png")
```
Output goes to `tmp/capybara/`.

## Performance

Feature specs are slow — write them for golden-path coverage only. Edge cases belong in request specs or unit specs.

examples.snippet: has_css?("[data-test-id=patient-row]", text: patient.email)
has_css?("[data-test-id=patient-john@example-com]")

rules.title: Request specs: HTTP coverage, real services, stub only external boundaries
rules.rule:
## Request Specs for HTTP Coverage

All new API HTTP coverage must be written as **request specs** in `spec/requests/`, not controller specs. Controller specs are soft-deprecated (legacy, don't add new ones). The spec type is auto-inferred from the directory (`infer_spec_type_from_file_location!`), so placing files in `spec/requests/` is sufficient.

**Differences:**
- Controller spec: dispatches by action symbol (`get :show`), isolates controller, bypasses routing/middleware — legacy.
- Request spec: dispatches by URL path (`get "/…"`), exercises full stack (routing → middleware → controller → rendered response), asserts status/body/side-effects.

## Mock Only True External Boundaries

Let requests hit the **real** Postgres/Redis/Typesense containers. Stub **only** genuine external services the test can't reach — third-party APIs and cloud SDKs that make an outbound network call. Examples of boundaries to stub:
- AWS SDK clients — Bedrock (vector-search embeddings), S3, SES, SQS, etc.
- Payment / billing gateways.
- Any other outbound third-party HTTP API.

**Stub at the boundary** (the SDK client or HTTP transport) — never the internal app classes that wrap it. Prove behaviour by asserting the boundary call **was / wasn't** made (`have_received` on a stubbed SDK client, or WebMock's `have_been_requested`).

### Example — stub an AWS SDK call (S3)

AWS SDK clients have built-in stub mode. Enable it, inject the stubbed client, and spy with `and_call_original` so the call returns the canned response but can be asserted:

ruby
s3 = Aws::S3::Client.new(stub_responses: true)
s3.stub_responses(:get_object, body: "file body")
allow(Aws::S3::Client).to receive(:new).and_return(s3)
allow(s3).to receive(:get_object).and_call_original     # spy — still returns the stubbed body

get "/downloads/report.pdf", headers: auth_headers

expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
expect(s3).to have_received(:get_object)                # the external S3 call happened
``n
Same shape for any AWS client (`Aws::BedrockRuntime::Client`, `Aws::SES::Client`, …). Real example: `spec/requests/pt/api/typesense/proxy_controller_spec.rb`.

### Example — stub a third-party HTTP call (Faraday, etc.)

Outbound HTTP is stubbed with **WebMock** (the repo standard: `stub_request`, loaded in `spec/spec_helper.rb`). WebMock intercepts at the socket, *below* Faraday, so never stub Faraday or the app's client class — only the request. `.with` asserts the outgoing shape; `have_been_requested` asserts it fired:

ruby
stub = stub_request(:post, "https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts")
  .with(body: { properties: { email: "test@example.com" } }.to_)
  .to_return(status: 201, body: { id: "123" }.to_)

post "/some/action/that/calls/hubspot", params: { email: "test@example.com" }, headers: auth_headers

expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
expect(stub).to have_been_requested                     # the external HTTP call happened, with the expected body
``n
Net connections are disabled in tests (`WebMock.disable_net_connect!`), so an un-stubbed external call fails loudly. Real example: `spec/domains/hubspot/client_spec.rb`.

### Capturing forwarded bytes (rare Faraday exception)

Stub `Faraday` directly (`allow(Faraday).to receive(:new)`) *only* when the assertion must capture the exact bytes sent — e.g. proving a proxy forwards a malformed body unchanged, which WebMock's parsed matchers can't express. For everything else, use WebMock.

## Fixtures

Request bodies follow the Realistic-fixtures discipline in `../CLAUDE.md` — send every field the real client sends, not just the asserted ones.

examples.snippet:
# Wrong — controller spec (legacy)
RSpec.describe WidgetsController do
  it { get :show, params: { id: 1 } }
end

# Correct — request spec dispatches by URL path
RSpec.describe "Widgets API" do
  it "returns the widget" do
    get "/widgets/1", headers: auth_headers
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
  end
end

# Wrong — stubbing internal app wrapper class
allow(MyApp::S3Wrapper).to receive(:fetch).and_return("body")

# Correct — stub at the SDK boundary and spy
s3 = Aws::S3::Client.new(stub_responses: true)
s3.stub_responses(:get_object, body: "file body")
allow(Aws::S3::Client).to receive(:new).and_return(s3)
allow(s3).to receive(:get_object).and_call_original

# Wrong — stubbing Faraday or the app's HTTP client class
allow(MyApp::HubspotClient).to receive(:create_contact)

# Correct — WebMock at the socket level
stub = stub_request(:post, "https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts")
  .with(body: { properties: { email: "test@example.com" } }.to_)
  .to_return(status: 201, body: { id: "123" }.to_)

rules.title: Config Directory Conventions
rules.rule:
Conventions for `config/` areas: Flipper flags, `settings/` YAML, and `routes.rb`.

**Encrypted Credentials**
- `config/sops_credentials/` and `*.enc.yml` must never be catted or committed decrypted.

**Feature Flags (`flipper_flags.yml`)**
- Flag creation via Flipper UI is disabled. Define the flag here first: `name`, `actor`, `description`.
- Sync it to Flipper by running the `Maintenance::SyncFlipperFeatures` task (per region).
- Enable via the Flipper UI (boolean, per-actor, or percentage).
- `actor:` is a display label, not a gate. It only prefixes the description in the Flipper UI (`config/initializers/flipper.rb`); it does not restrict which actor types can be enabled or imply percentage rollout. Convention: `Global|Provider` means "per-region and per-provider".
- Flags are per-region — each region's Flipper state is independent; enabling in one region does nothing elsewhere.
- Registered groups `internal_users` and `e2e` (example.com emails) exist for staff-only rollouts.

**`settings/` YAML**
- Per-concern config files are read via `config_for("settings/<name>")` in `config/application.rb` and exposed as `Rails.application.config.<name>`.
- Region-scoped files (`typesense.yml`, `s3_buckets.yml`, `zoom.yml`, ...) nest env → region; boot picks the region with `.fetch(ENV.fetch("COUNTRY").to_sym)`.
- YAML anchors (`defaults: &defaults`, `<<: *defaults`) are resolved at boot — per-region keys override anchor defaults.
- Secrets come from sops credentials via ERB (`<%= Rails.application.credentials.dig(...) %>`); static non-secret values stay inline. Never put a secret literal in these files.

**`routes.rb`**
- Grape APIs are `mount`ed (e.g. `mount API::AcmeApp::V3::Root => "/api/physiapp/v3"`); plain controllers use `namespace`/`resources`.
